newsitem.title: FINLAND: POLL - Upward pressure seen holding on markka.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Upward pressure seen holding on markka.

text.p: Many economists expect the Finnish markka to stay under strong upward pressure in the short term, but by year-end the dust of speculative battle is widely expected to have settled, a Reuters poll shows.
In the poll of 15 economists on Friday, most respondents expected DEM/FIM to end 1997 near its 3.04 central parity rate against the mark in the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).

But asked how strong the markka can get this year, only four expected DEM/FIM to hold above the 2.97 area -- its notional floor assuming the Bank of Finland is targeting a 2.25 percent fluctuation band from its ERM mid-rate.
About one-third saw DEM/FIM firming to the 2.90-2.95 range, assuming all else was equal and no key rate moves occurred in major economies.

That would suggest the central bank, which on Friday said it was happy to have boosted its foreign currency reserves by nearly 16 billion markka in the week to January 15, is expected to face a tough battle to hold down the Finnish unit.
Analysts earlier this week said the risk of a key rate cut would only really kick in with DEM/FIM at 2.95, but some on Friday saw this happening already around 2.97.
"FIM in the near term will have the wind behind it and could do well, but I think it would have difficulty breaking 2.95," said Keld Holm at Lehman Brothers in London.

Economists arguing for a "fair value" for the markka at current levels around 2.97-98 stressed the longer-term perspective: any current undervaluation of the currency would just cancel out a past period of overvaluation.
Others noted that Finland needs an undervalued markka to keep generating current account surpluses to service debt.
Some said the central bank should have an easier time arresting the markka's rise than if it were trying to put the brakes on an overvalued currency.

"I think it is easier for the Bank of Finland to keep the lid on the markka when the tendency is to appreciate -- if it were on a weakening trend, the Bank of Finland may lose the game," said Matti Huomo, chief economist at OKOBank.

But economists agree that overseas investors, facing scant opportunities in forex markets as a whole, are moving into markka on the assumption that it, in the wake of the Norwegian crown, can be a winner in the rally against the German mark.
"The rate is tending stronger and stronger and that could last weeks or months," said another overseas economist -- although he expected the markka to end 1997 little changed.
Besides the figures, the tone of comments made privately by market operators suggests a tough fight is on, and will continue to demand heavy influence and discretion from the central bank.

"It is a big fight," said one overseas economist after the bank admitted it had intervened to brake the markka's rise. "But if you put up too much of a fight you will only make people come back to test your resolve again."
The following summarises the 15 responses, most of which were collected on Friday before the central bank announced the reserves increase:
Q: Where do you see DEM/FIM at year-end?
Median: 3.00 - 3.04 (9 respondents)
Q: Where do you see the markka at its strongest this year?
2.70 - 2.85: 3 respondents
2.90 - 2.95: 6 respondents
Over 2.95 : 5 respondents, of which four see DEM/FIM
staying above 2.97

Poll respondents: ABB Treasury Centre Finland, Alfred Berg, Interbank, Kemira Treasury, Kesko Treasury, Lehman Brothers, Merita Bank, Morgan Stanley, OKOBank, Postipankki, Protos, SE Banken, Selin Finance, Unibank, one anonymous. (One gave no answer to question two.)
